page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 1 vCPU and 4.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates a single dedicated physical core with one thread. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-standard-1 in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1088.79 is categorized as weak, while the multi-core score of 1088.79 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is similarly limited, with read-only large block speeds at 10.68 GB/sec and write speeds at 9.71 GB/sec. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 895.0 and a multi-core score of 898.0, reflecting its entry-level computational capability.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require high resource density or rapid processing. Tradeoffs include poor database operations performance with 437.87 on Passmark and low static web serving throughput of 1.21 GB/sec. It is best suited for lightweight background utilities, basic testing, or low-traffic web serving where minimal CPU and memory resources are sufficient.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is an entry-level general-purpose instance configured with 1 vCPU and 4.0 GB of RAM. It operates on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor at 2.3 GHz with a single dedicated physical core and no hyperthreading. The instance features no local storage, no bundled GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Performance benchmarks consistently rank in the bottom 10% to 25% across CPU, memory, and database tests, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1088.79 and a Passmark database operations score of 437.87. Qualitatively, the n1-standard-1 offers a cost-effective option for low-resource tasks, though it presents significant performance tradeoffs for demanding applications. It is best suited for basic general-purpose workloads, lightweight background processes, and simple testing environments.
